literal: The small refusal of wealthy people possessing excellence has the nature of being like the rain-cloud experiencing intense dryness.
translation: The brief refusal of truly noble and wealthy people to give is like a rain-cloud temporarily running dry.
modern: சிறப்புடைய செல்வர்களது தற்காலிகமான வெறுப்பு அல்லது கொடாமை, மழைமேகம் வறட்சி அடைந்ததைப் போன்ற தன்மையுடையது.
explanation: This couplet explains the nature of generous people even when they temporarily stop giving. The 'small refusal' (ciṟutuni) of noble, wealthy individuals (cīruṭaic celvar) is not due to miserliness, but is a temporary phase. It is compared to a rain-cloud (māri) that has run dry (vaṟaṅkūrntu) for a brief period. Just as a dry cloud will eventually fill up and pour rain again, these noble souls will resume their benevolence once their temporary limitations pass.
